sources.entry: VPN Bypass - Menu bar app to route specific domains and services around your VPN. [![Open-Source Software][OSS Icon]](https://github.com/GeiserX/VPN-Bypass) ![Freeware][Freeware Icon]
VPN Bypass - Route specific domains and services around your corporate VPN while keeping the rest of your traffic protected.

summary.one_liner: VPN Bypass is a macOS menu bar app that routes chosen domains, services and subnets around (or, in another mode, only through) a corporate VPN and reapplies those routes when the VPN or network changes.
summary.what_it_does: The app runs from the macOS menu bar and offers three routing modes: Bypass sends listed destinations around the VPN, VPN Only sends only those destinations through it, and Custom lets each rule pick a route with first match winning. It ships 37 built-in service packs (such as Telegram, YouTube, Netflix, Spotify, Zoom and GitHub) and accepts custom domains, wildcards and subnets. In Custom mode a rule can exit direct, through a specific VPN, through an HTTP or SOCKS5 proxy, or through a Tailscale peer. The README says it detects a list of VPN clients including GlobalProtect, Cisco AnyConnect, OpenVPN, WireGuard, FortiClient, Zscaler, Cloudflare WARP, Pulse Secure, Check Point and Tailscale. Routes are restored automatically on reconnect, and domains are re-resolved as their addresses change. A `vpnb` command-line tool controls the app over a socket restricted to the user's account, and an MCP server is documented separately.
use_cases: bypass corporate VPN for streaming video
keep AirPlay or Chromecast working on VPN
route personal traffic around work VPN
split tunnel on macOS without client support
send only certain domains through VPN
manage VPN routes from the menu bar
how_to_run: Open VPN Bypass from Applications and approve the one admin prompt that installs the root helper
Connect the VPN, then enable a service in Settings > Services or type a domain into the dropdown
notable: Three routing modes: Bypass, VPN Only and Custom with first-match rules
Custom rules can exit via a specific VPN, HTTP/SOCKS5 proxy, or Tailscale peer
No kernel or system extension; a small root helper handles routing
vpnb CLI and a separate MCP server let scripts or AI agents control the app
Optional /etc/hosts DNS bypass and config import/export
caveats: Needs an admin approval to install the root helper
Installing via Homebrew requires the extra 'brew trust' step shown in the README
keywords: keep personal traffic off work network
